topic.subject: physics
topic.title: Pressure, density and fluids
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26 Applying Forces; TGS 2026-27 pressure and density
topic.overview: Pressure describes how concentrated a force is over an area. Density compares mass with volume. Together they help explain deep-water pressure, floating and many design choices.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: One pascal is one newton per square metre: 1 Pa = 1 N/m2.
For the same force, smaller area gives larger pressure.
Pressure in a liquid increases with depth because more liquid is above.
Use compatible units: kg/m3 or g/cm3.
In a particle model, greater mass packed into the same volume means greater density.
An object tends to float if its average density is lower than the fluid and sink if higher.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: the SI unit of pressure, equal to N/m2
a liquid or gas that can flow
the space occupied by an object or substance
the upward force a fluid exerts on an immersed object
remain supported at a fluid surface when forces balance
move down through a fluid when weight exceeds supporting effects

workedExamples.prompt: A 600 N force acts over 0.20 m2. Calculate pressure.
A block has mass 240 g and volume 80 cm3. Calculate density.

practicals.title: Determine density of an irregular solid
practicals.aim: Measure the density of a small irregular object.
practicals.variables: Measure mass and displaced-water volume; repeat volume readings where possible.
practicals.method: Measure mass on a tared balance; record initial cylinder volume; fully submerge object without splashing; record final volume; calculate displacement and density.
practicals.expectedResult: Density equals mass divided by displaced volume.
practicals.safety: Do not drop objects into glassware; wipe spills; use a thread and choose a non-reactive, non-porous object.
practicals.evaluation: Use a narrow graduated cylinder with finer scale, read meniscus at eye level, remove bubbles and repeat.

commonMistakes: Multiplying force by area for pressure.
Mixing grams with cubic metres without conversion.
Saying pressure is greater at depth because water is denser there in the simple incompressible model.
examTips: Write equation, substitute, answer and unit.
For area effects, state 'same force' before comparing pressure.
Density is about mass per volume, not simply whether an object feels heavy.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.title: Determine density of an irregular solid
practicals.aim: Measure the density of a small irregular object.
practicals.variables: Measure mass and displaced-water volume; repeat volume readings where possible.
practicals.method: Measure mass on a tared balance; record initial cylinder volume; fully submerge object without splashing; record final volume; calculate displacement and density.
practicals.expectedResult: Density equals mass divided by displaced volume.
practicals.safety: Do not drop objects into glassware; wipe spills; use a thread and choose a non-reactive, non-porous object.
practicals.evaluation: Use a narrow graduated cylinder with finer scale, read meniscus at eye level, remove bubbles and repeat.
